item.title: Katsina suspends Emir of Daura’s engagements over assault allegation, launches investigation
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina The Katsina State Government has constituted an investigative committee to probe allegations of sexual assault involving the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Umar Faruk Umar, and a foreign tourist. The government also announced the suspension of the traditional ruler’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation. The decisions were contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Dr Bala Salisu Zango, on behalf of the state government. According to the statement, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda expressed serious concern over the allegations, describing the matter as one requiring careful attention and appropriate action. The governor consequently directed the immediate constitution of an investigative committee to examine the allegations and advise the government on the appropriate course of action. The statement said the decision was informed by the seriousness of the allegations and the need to establish the facts surrounding the reported incident. The government assured the public that justice would be served, adding that the findings and recommendations of the committee would be fully implemented. It said the suspension of the Emir’s official engagements and travels was among the measures taken by the government while the investigation lasted. The government also appealed to residents and members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and refrain from actions capable of disrupting public peace. It urged residents to continue with their normal activities, reaffirming its commitment to handling the matter appropriately. The outcome of the committee’s investigation is expected to guide further action by the state government. item.title: Man Utd win appeal over Yoro red card
item.description: Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in Manchester United’s 4-0 mauling by Liverpool has been overturned, the Football Association announced on Tuesday. The French defender was dismissed in the eighth minute at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak as he advanced towards goal, with referee Sam Barrott deciding Yoro had denied an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United indicated on Monday that they intended to appeal for wrongful dismissal and a one-match suspension for the centre-back has now been lifted. The FA said the written reasons for their decision would be published in due course. Yoro, 21, will now be available for Saturday’s 1500 GMT kick-off against Brentford at Old Trafford. Dominik Szoboszlai scored Liverpool’s opening goal directly from the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s challenge and the home team cantered to an easy win. One question raised over the Yoro incident was whether Isak had the ball sufficiently under control for it to count as denial of an obvious goalscoring opportunity. United captain Bruno Fernandes told the BBC after the match that it was “never a red card”, adding: “I think it’s too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever. “To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it’s not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game.” Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tenure got off to the worst possible start at Anfield, with a defeat that keeps them in the Premier League relegation zone after just one top-flight win all season. item.title: NAFDAC faults Edo committee over drug seizures, business closures
item.description: Seeks Okpebholo’s intervention over Arden Table Water By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has faulted the Edo State Consumer Protection Committee (ESCPC) over the alleged seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of business premises and imposition of fines on operators without proper regulatory authorisation. The agency also appealed to Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo, to intervene in the reported shutdown of Chepfets Mega Investment Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Arden Table Water, insisting that the product’s registration was undergoing renewal and that this did not establish that it was unsafe or substandard. The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, raised the concerns while clarifying the agency’s position on the committee’s activities in the state. She expressed concern over reports that the committee had been using NAFDAC’s product authentication platforms to verify regulated products and make public declarations about their authenticity and quality. Adeyeye explained that access to the agency’s authentication platforms did not automatically confer regulatory authority on users or provide the technical basis for declaring products counterfeit, adulterated, injurious, safe or unsafe. NAFDAC said it recognised the importance of consumer protection and welcomed collaboration with state governments and other stakeholders in the fight against counterfeit, falsified, adulterated and substandard products. However, it stressed that such interventions must respect established regulatory boundaries and applicable laws. The agency said it was particularly concerned by reports that the committee had seized regulated products, publicly labelled some products fake or adulterated, sealed business premises and imposed fines on operators under the guise of working for NAFDAC without its authorisation or guidance. It also raised concerns over the reported deployment of NAFDAC’s Automated Product Administration and Monitoring System (NAPAMS), QR code scanner, Short Messaging Service (SMS) verification platform and other regulatory tools by the committee to assess products and make public pronouncements on their identity, authenticity, efficacy and effectiveness. According to the agency, failed QR code scans, missing registration details or inconsistencies in product packaging do not, on their own, constitute sufficient evidence that a product is counterfeit or substandard. It advised consumers and other stakeholders to report such irregularities to NAFDAC for investigation and possible laboratory analysis, urging the public to await the agency’s findings before making claims about products. On the reported enforcement activities, NAFDAC condemned what it described as the unilateral seizure of pharmaceutical products, closure of establishments and imposition of fines by the committee. item.title: Ajaokuta must work again, Kogi won’t be neglected – Atiku
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, develop Idah River Port and complete the Kabba-Egbe road, promising to address longstanding infrastructure challenges across Kogi State. Speaking at his campaign rally in Lokoja, Atiku outlined development projects for the state’s three senatorial districts, including improved roads and water supply in Kogi East. He said the plans were aimed at creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and making life more affordable for residents. According to the Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said his proposed interventions would focus on turning the state’s economic potential into tangible benefits for its people. Addressing residents of Kogi East, he pledged to improve rural infrastructure and develop Idah River Port to ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand business opportunities. “To my brothers and sisters in Kogi East, I know what it means when a farmer cannot get produce to market because the road has failed, or when a family must struggle every day for clean water. We will improve your roads and water supply, and develop Idah River Port so that the region’s farmers and businesses can reach more customers,” he said. For Kogi Central, Atiku promised to revive the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, with a focus on restoring industrial production and creating employment. “Ajaokuta must finally become a working steel mill. I want its furnaces working, its gates open to skilled workers and its promise felt in the homes of the people who have waited so long. We will also support the roads and services that allow surrounding communities to benefit from that industry,” he said. In Kogi West, he pledged to complete the Kabba-Egbe road, which he said should no longer remain an unfulfilled promise. “The Kabba to Egbe road cannot remain an endless promise. We will complete it and make travel and trade easier for the communities along its route,” he stated. At the national level, Atiku also pledged to pursue the dredging of Baro Port and restore a targeted subsidy on fuel refined in Nigeria, saying the measures would help reduce transportation and production costs. The proposals formed part of his broader promise to translate infrastructure development and the state’s economic resources into employment and improved living conditions. item.title: Atiku has youth support despite Tinubu’s control of Lagos, says Momodu
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) chieftain Dele Momodu has defended former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s appeal to young voters, saying Atiku has never controlled a state while President Bola Tinubu exercises strong political influence in Lagos. Momodu spoke in an interview on Arise Television on Tuesday, discussing Atiku’s chances in the 2027 election, age dynamics, political influence and efforts by opposition parties to agree on a consensus candidate. “If he’s not connecting to the youths, you won’t see people shouting ‘Bamayi’ all over Nigeria. I just watched your programme now in Kogi State. The people on the streets are not geriatrics; they are young people,” he said. The ADC chieftain argued that age should not be used to judge a candidate’s ability to connect with voters. Citing his own presidential bid, he said: “I contested 15 years ago, at the age of 51 to be president of Nigeria. Why didn’t I win? It’s not about age.” He said Atiku was surrounded by young supporters and described him as “a completely detribalised Nigerian” and “an employer of labour.” Comparing Atiku’s political influence with Tinubu’s, Momodu said, “He has never held on to any state. Tinubu controls Lagos, life and death. Tinubu controls Lagos and Atiku does not control anywhere.” On talks to select a consensus opposition candidate, Momodu pointed to Atiku’s past willingness to step aside for another candidate. “In 1993, I was 33 years old when Alhaji Atiku Abubakar first came out to run as a potential candidate of SDP, and at that time, he stepped down for MKO Abiola without making any trouble. After that, he was expected to be the running mate, he didn’t get it. He never fought anybody. He then contested in his state and became governor before they now made him running mate to President Olusegun Obasanjo. He has pursued his dreams with uncommon equanimity,” he said. item.title: NDC Boycotts IGP’s Meeting Over Alleged Attacks On Members
item.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has announced its decision to boycott a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, citing alleged attacks on its members and what it described as the police’s failure to protect opposition figures. The party said it no longer felt safe under the Nigeria Police Force, accusing security agencies of failing to prevent repeated attacks on its members allegedly carried out by thugs loyal to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). The NDC announced its position in a statement signed by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, on Monday. It said it would not legitimise a security process that had failed to protect its members, adding that the alleged violence had become an intolerable pattern across the country. The party cited incidents in Benue, Edo, Calabar, Enugu and Delta states, including an alleged attempt by APC loyalists to prevent its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, from entering Benue State. It accused the APC-led government of turning political campaigns into battlefields, where the safety of opposition members could no longer be guaranteed. The NDC also alleged that security personnel were complicit in the violence, particularly the alleged attack on the campaign team of its Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State. Omo-Agege is a chieftain of the NDC. Gunmen reportedly attacked Omo-Agege’s campaign convoy in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area. The former deputy senate president escaped unhurt, according to his media adviser, Sunny Areh. The attack initially left four campaign members dead, according to the Omo-Agege Campaign Organisation. However, the Nigeria Police Force said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed, while several others sustained injuries. Police Speak The police, in a statement issued on Tuesday by its Force Public Relations Officer, said an investigation had been launched to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and determine the verified casualty figure. Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, directed the Delta State Commissioner of Police to conduct a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation. The police said the investigation would examine the sequence of events, identify those responsible and establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of officers at the scene. It added that any officer found to have acted negligently or breached professional standards would face disciplinary action, while anyone found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The NDC, however, accused the police of displaying bias and failing to investigate previous attacks on its members or bring those responsible to justice. item.title: CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has explained why it overturned the Confederation of African Football’s (CAF) decision to award Morocco the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, ruling that Senegal’s 1-0 victory in the final must stand. In a media release on Tuesday, the court said both teams had returned to the pitch and expressed their willingness to continue before the referee, Jean-Jacques Ndala, blew his whistle to resume play in the 109th minute. It explained that the referee’s decision to restart or stop the match fell within his authority, adding that the effects of his decision were limited to the pitch and therefore covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine. “After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee’s decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” the statement said. CAS also ruled that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, relied upon by Morocco in its challenge, did not apply to the circumstances of the final. According to the court, the provisions are intended to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to abandon the game permanently. The court further rejected the description of the referee’s decision as ‘arbitrary’, acknowledging the extreme tension surrounding the match but stating that his judgment did not appear to have been influenced by external factors. Consequently, CAS upheld the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF), set aside the CAF Appeal Board’s decision and reinstated the decision of CAF’s Disciplinary Board. The ruling confirms Senegal’s 1-0 victory over Morocco in the January 18 final, restoring the West African nation as AFCON 2025 champions. CAF had previously declared Senegal to have forfeited the final after the team temporarily left the pitch in protest during the match, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory. The decision was unanimous among the three-member CAS panel. The post CAS explains decision to restore Senegal’s AFCON title appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ASUP declares two-week strike in four states over unpaid allowances
item.description: Accuses Enugu govt of neglecting lecturers’ welfare since 2014 By Chinedu Adonu The Academic Staff Union of Polytechnics (ASUP), Zone D, has directed its chapters in Enugu, Imo, Edo and Cross River states to embark on a two-week warning strike over the failure of the respective state governments to implement the 2026 renegotiated agreement between the union and the Federal Government. The union also directed chapters that have yet to join the ongoing industrial action to commence the strike immediately, warning that failure to address its demands could result in an indefinite shutdown of academic activities in the affected institutions. ASUP Zone D, which covers the South-East and South-South geopolitical zones, announced the directive at a press briefing in Enugu on Tuesday by its Zonal Coordinator, Comrade Dr Iloma U. Richard. The union said the strike followed the failure of the affected state governments to implement the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA), Earned Academic Allowance (EAA) and other components of the ASUP/FGN 2026 renegotiated agreement. It recalled that the Federal Government and ASUP signed the agreement on April 8, 2026, with implementation of the allowances taking effect from January 2026. According to the union, while the Federal Government has commenced implementation of the agreement for lecturers in federal polytechnics, several state governments have failed to extend the benefits to academic staff in their institutions. It said its national leadership had written to state governors on August 10 and September 21, 2026, appealing for the implementation of the allowances but received disappointing responses from some states. The union said the National Executive Council, at its 118th regular meeting held on October 22 in Abuja, subsequently issued a 15-day ultimatum to the affected state governments, beginning October 27, to address the matter. “Having exhaustively explored measures to persuade concerned states to comply, the national leadership was constrained to direct all chapters in the states that were yet to comply to proceed on strike with effect from November 12, 2026,” the union said. ASUP, however, noted that some states had responded positively, listing Yobe, Kano, Ondo, Bayelsa, Niger, Abia, Taraba, Plateau, Nasarawa, Zamfara, Jigawa and Rivers as states that had approved the implementation of CATA and EAA. It added that engagements with Delta, Akwa Ibom and Katsina states were also progressing positively. Enugu lecturers’ welfare Beyond the allowances, the union expressed particular concern over what it described as years of neglect of academic staff welfare in Enugu State-owned institutions, particularly the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, and Enugu State Polytechnic, Iwollo. It alleged that lecturers in the two institutions were yet to benefit from the prevailing minimum wage, wage awards and the 35 per cent and 25 per cent salary reviews approved in 2023. item.title: Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles
item.description: Egypt remain the most successful country in the history of the Africa Cup of Nations, AFCON with seven titles, followed by Cameroon and Ghana, who have won the continental competition five and four times respectively. Nigeria are among five countries in the top four positions, having lifted the trophy three times since making their debut at the tournament. The Super Eagles won their first AFCON title in 1980, when Nigeria hosted the competition and defeated Algeria 3-0 in the final. They secured their second crown in Tunisia in 1994, beating Zambia 2-1, before claiming their third title in South Africa in 2013 with a 1-0 victory over Burkina Faso. Côte d’Ivoire are also three-time champions, having won the tournament in 1992, 2015 and 2023. Egypt lead the all-time standings with seven titles, having dominated the competition in its early years and later enjoyed a remarkable run of three consecutive championships in 2006, 2008 and 2010. Cameroon occupy second place with five titles, while Ghana are third with four. Ghana’s last triumph came in 1982, while Cameroon’s most recent success was in 2017. Algeria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have each won the competition twice. Algeria claimed their titles in 1990 and 2019, while DR Congo won in 1968 and 1974, when the country competed under the names Congo-Kinshasa and Zaire. Morocco are also credited with two titles, following the Confederation of African Football’s March 2026 decision to award them the 2025 AFCON trophy. Senegal had initially won the final 1-0 after extra time, but CAF’s Appeal Board later ruled that the Senegalese team had forfeited the match and recorded a 3-0 victory for Morocco. Senegal subsequently appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, which was expected to issue its ruling on November 24, 2026. The outcome of that appeal could affect the official title record. Seven other countries have won the AFCON title once. They are Ethiopia, Sudan, Congo, South Africa, Tunisia, Zambia and Senegal. Below is the ranking of countries by the number of AFCON titles won: Egypt – 7 titles: 1957, 1959, 1986, 1998, 2006, 2008 and 2010. Cameroon – 5 titles: 1984, 1988, 2000, 2002 and 2017. Ghana – 4 titles: 1963, 1965, 1978 and 1982. Nigeria – 3 titles: 1980, 1994 and 2013. Côte d’Ivoire – 3 titles: 1992, 2015 and 2023. Algeria – 2 titles: 1990 and 2019. DR Congo – 2 titles: 1968 and 1974 Senegal – 2 titles: 2021, 2025 Ethiopia – 1 title: 1962. Sudan – 1 title: 1970. Congo – 1 title: 1972. South Africa – 1 title: 1996. Tunisia – 1 title: 2004. Zambia – 1 title: 2012. Morocco – 1 title: 1976 Vanguard News The post Full List: 10 countries with most AFCON titles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I’ll continue to criticise Atiku for attacking Tinubu – Shettima
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Vice-President Kashim Shettima has defended his right to criticise African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, saying he would not hold back in defending President Bola Tinubu against political attacks. Shettima, who described Atiku as an elder statesman whom he holds in high regard, said their political differences would not prevent him from expressing his views about the former vice-president. He spoke on Tuesday in Maiduguri, Borno State’s capital, during the inauguration of the North-East Development Commission’s multi-sectoral development interventions. “We respect former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. He is an elder statesman we hold in very high esteem, but as a Fulani man, I have the right to throw stones at him. And he has to endure strictly whatever stones I throw at him,” he said. The vice president also cautioned against attempts to portray political disagreements as personal hostility, saying he was willing to maintain cordial relationships with opposition figures as long as they did not attack his principal. “So long as they do not attack my boss, we will practise politics of maturity, politics without bitterness, and politics of tolerance because what binds us together surpasses whatever that divides us,” he said. Shettima also identified former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi and former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his friends, while describing Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde as a personal friend. He said he had never insulted Makinde, adding that political differences should not undermine relationships among leaders. The vice-president urged Nigerians to make informed decisions ahead of the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the Tinubu administration’s economic policies were beginning to yield results. Shettima also ruled out a return to petrol subsidy, saying its removal and the realignment of multiple exchange rates were necessary to prevent the economy from collapsing. “The president has a great deal of human empathy for the Nigerian people. He withdrew the subsidy, not to inflict pain on Nigerians. No, he removed the subsidy to save the Nigerian economy from collapse,” he said. He further accused some Nigerians who had benefited from the previous economic arrangements of sponsoring anti-government sentiments. Calling for restraint among political actors, Shettima urged candidates to accept the outcome of the 2027 election rather than resort to threats and actions capable of creating tension. He expressed confidence that Nigerians would vote massively for Tinubu on January 16, adding that there were no polling booths on Facebook, Instagram or other social media platforms. item.title: Senate orders scrutiny of revised 2025 laws
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has called for a thorough scrutiny of the revised and consolidated Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2025, to ensure accuracy before granting legislative approval. The President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, made the call on Tuesday while reading a letter from President Bola Tinubu seeking the National Assembly’s approval of the revised compendium. Akpabio said the Senate must ensure that all amendments were accurately reflected and that no provisions had been altered from the original laws passed by the National Assembly. He said it was necessary to compare the compiled laws with the versions passed by both chambers to prevent discrepancies that could undermine the country’s legal framework. In the letter, Tinubu said the committee constituted on October 24, 2024, examined 932 federal enactments and 731 subsidiary legislations. He disclosed that 664 principal enactments were validated for inclusion in the revised compendium, while 268 were identified as obsolete, spent or repealed. According to the President, the updated compendium would provide a reliable legal reference for the judiciary, legal practitioners, government institutions, investors and the general public. The Senate subsequently referred the revised compendium to the Committees on Rules and Business and Judiciary for further legislative action. Contributing to the debate, former Senate Leader, Senator Yahaya Abdullahi (APC, Kebbi North), described the exercise as important to Nigeria’s legal system and the administration of justice. He recalled that a similar exercise was conducted after the return to democratic governance in 1999 to give legitimacy to decrees enacted under military administrations. Abdullahi, who noted that the last official consolidation of the laws was undertaken in 2004, said the current exercise had become necessary after more than two decades. He, however, cautioned against rushing the process, given its implications for the country’s legal system and justice delivery. He proposed that the compendium be thoroughly examined by the Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, with the support of competent legal experts. According to him, the committee should analyse the volumes and present a comprehensive report to enable lawmakers to understand the proposed changes before approval. Also contributing, Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), supported the call for scrutiny, warning that even a single altered clause could make the compilation inconsistent with the laws passed by the National Assembly. Barau recommended that the consolidated provisions be compared with the original versions passed by both chambers and those assented to by the President. Akpabio agreed with the submissions, saying the Senate usually engaged consultants and relevant experts to examine such documents before presenting a summarised report. item.title: Reps advance bills to reform social investment agency, regulate eye care
item.description: By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed two bills seeking to reform Nigeria’s social investment programmes and strengthen the regulation of optometry and dispensing opticians through second reading. The bills, sponsored by Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu and other lawmakers, are aimed at improving the delivery of social protection programmes and addressing regulatory gaps in the country’s eye care sector. Leading the debate on the proposed amendment to the National Social Investment Programme Agency (Establishment) Act, 2023, Kalu said the success of social investment programmes should be measured not by the size of their budgets or the number of initiatives introduced, but by their actual impact on vulnerable Nigerians. He described social investment as a commitment by the Nigerian state to prevent temporary hardship from becoming permanent exclusion. The Deputy Speaker said the growing scale and complexity of Nigeria’s social protection system had made it necessary to strengthen the institutional framework for coordinating, implementing and monitoring interventions. According to him, the proposed amendment would address administrative fragmentation, duplication of beneficiaries, unreliable data and inadequate coordination among the different levels of government. Among its major provisions is the introduction of the Grant for Vulnerable Groups Programme and the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as components of the agency. The bill also seeks to establish the National Social Safety-Net Coordinating Office as the central institution for coordinating and managing data on national social safety nets, including maintaining, updating and verifying the National Social Register. Kalu said the proposed legislation would also provide for the establishment of state offices to bring programme implementation closer to beneficiaries and introduce executive directors with clearly defined responsibilities for individual programmes. He explained that the changes would strengthen accountability, improve coordination and ensure that government assistance reached intended beneficiaries. He identified children requiring support to remain in school, unemployed youths seeking economic opportunities and vulnerable households needing temporary assistance as some of those expected to benefit from a more coordinated social investment system. The 15-clause bill was subsequently subjected to a voice vote by the Speaker, Abbas Tajudeen, and received the support of lawmakers. In a related development, the House also passed second reading a bill seeking to repeal the Optometrists and Dispensing Opticians (Registration, etc.) Act, Cap. 09, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, and introduce a new regulatory framework for the profession. item.title: Senegal Regain AFCON Title After Appeal
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. “The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025,” CAS said in a statement. The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal’s appeal had been upheld by “a unanimous decision”, and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless. Senegal and Morocco players line up prior the Africa Cup of Nations (CAN) final football match between Senegal and Morocco at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat on January 18, 2026. Photo by PAUL ELLIS / AFP The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations. Those state that if a team “refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition”. However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on. The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee’s decision to restart the final showed that “the conditions for resuming the match had been met”, and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore “not applicable in this case”. item.title: 2027 polls: NUC considers four-week university break
item.description: …Mobilises VCs to support INEC as commission plans 57,000 additional BVAS machines By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The National Universities Commission (NUC) is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics to participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections. The proposed adjustment is part of efforts by the commission to mobilise Vice-Chancellors and university authorities nationwide to provide credible and non-partisan academic personnel, particularly as Collation and Returning Officers. The NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, led a delegation of National Commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the commission. Ribadu said the NUC would engage Vice-Chancellors on the nomination of qualified academics for electoral assignments, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process. He also pledged to issue a formal circular to universities upon receiving an official request from INEC, stressing that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend significantly on the integrity of personnel deployed to conduct them. “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel,” he said. The NUC boss explained that the proposed adjustment of academic calendars would give academics sufficient time to discharge their electoral responsibilities without compromising students’ academic programmes. According to him, the proposed break would not exceed four weeks, adding that the commission would consult university administrators to ensure that the arrangement neither disrupted academic activities nor interfered with INEC’s electoral timetable. “We will discuss with the Vice-Chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he said. Ribadu also stressed that academics and other ad hoc officials engaged in the electoral process must demonstrate absolute neutrality, proposing that they take an oath of neutrality before deployment. Beyond providing election officials, the NUC Executive Secretary proposed a broader institutional partnership between universities and INEC, including student internship opportunities at the electoral commission, joint research initiatives and possible academic programmes in electoral studies. He identified artificial intelligence, robotics and data analytics as areas where Nigerian universities could collaborate with INEC to strengthen electoral administration and improve the country’s democratic process. The NUC also proposed leveraging student organisations, campus clubs and other university platforms to intensify voter education and combat misinformation and disinformation ahead of the elections. item.title: Delta killings: Turaki-led PDP urges presidency to renounce ‘war rhetoric’ ahead of 2027
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee (INWC) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has blamed President Bola Tinubu’s past political statements for what it described as a growing climate of violence against opposition parties, following the killing of at least four persons in an attack on a Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign in Delta State. The group said the attack in Uduere, Ughelli North, where gunmen opened fire while former Deputy Senate President and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, was addressing supporters, exposed the dangers of inflammatory political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Ini Ememobong, on Tuesday, the INWC demanded that Tinubu publicly renounce his previous remarks, which it accused of encouraging hostility towards opposition parties. The statement cited Tinubu’s 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with”, as well as his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”, as examples of what it described as dangerous political messaging. “These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties,” it alleged. It also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party. On Delta State, the group alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups had occurred in November alone. It further alleged that the incidents were widely believed to have been sponsored by the APC. “With this latest attack and the deaths and injuries it caused, the world can now clearly see the fruits of the evil seed planted by the APC through violent communication,” the statement said. The INWC also demanded a thorough and transparent investigation into the attack, urging the police to make their findings public. It called on the Inspector-General of Police to ensure that the investigation he ordered was conducted professionally and that other political attacks across the country received similar attention. It urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), the National Peace Committee and election observers to identify and publicly expose individuals responsible for political violence, including through international platforms. The group also raised concerns over allegations that police personnel were present at the scene but failed to assist victims, calling on security agencies, particularly the police, to demonstrate neutrality and professionalism. “Nigerians need responsible leadership that does not sacrifice the peace and unity of the country at the altar of political domination and elections,” it said.

item.title: NYSC warns Bayelsa corps members against night movements, politicians
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in Bayelsa State has warned corps members deployed to the state to avoid late-night movements, compromising situations and unnecessary exposure to security risks. The State Coordinator, Mr Samuel Pepple, gave the warning on Tuesday during the low-key closing ceremony of the 2026 Batch C Stream II orientation course at the NYSC Permanent Orientation Camp, Boro Town, Kolokuma-Opokuma Local Government Area. Pepple urged the departing corps members to uphold discipline, remain security-conscious and demonstrate integrity as they proceed to their respective Places of Primary Assignment (PPAs). He advised them to embrace their postings, particularly those assigned to rural and riverine communities, assuring them of adequate security arrangements, decent accommodation and necessary safety equipment, including life jackets for those deployed to riverine areas. Emphasising personal safety, the coordinator urged the corps members to communicate their whereabouts to trusted persons and strictly adhere to security guidelines provided during the orientation course. On electoral responsibilities, Pepple warned them against political interference, inducements and other actions capable of compromising their integrity. He stressed that corps members must remain politically neutral and discharge any electoral responsibilities assigned to them with professionalism and patriotism. The state coordinator also encouraged them to integrate into their host communities, respect local cultures and traditions, and contribute meaningfully to the development of their areas of deployment. He noted that their services were particularly needed in rural and riverine communities, where access to essential services, especially education, remained limited. Reminding them that the orientation course was only the first phase of their service year, Pepple directed the corps members to report promptly to their PPAs after completing the necessary documentation. He also instructed them to obtain approval before embarking on any journey outside their places of primary assignment. Pepple expressed confidence in their ability to contribute meaningfully to national development, urging them to serve with courage, commitment and selflessness. He concluded by praying for their safety and a successful service year, wishing them journey mercies as they departed the camp for their respective places of primary assignment. item.title: 2027: Again, Atiku vows to restore subsidy; revive Ajaokuta steel mill
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has renewed his pledge to restore fuel subsidy and promised to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge at the ADC presidential campaign rally in Lokoja, Kogi State, on Tuesday, while restating his commitment to making life more affordable and creating jobs and prosperity through industrial investment. “Our leadership in the previous years have not met the aspirations of the people of Kogi State. I have already promised Nigerians that I will return subsidy. I want to let you know that I mean it. I am serious about it, and I am sincere about it. This will bring about affordability of your life,” Atiku said. He also pledged to revive and complete the Ajaokuta Steel Mill, saying foreign investment could fund the project without public spending. “Secondly, for me in particular, I want to promise you here today that I will revive and complete the Ajaokuta steel mill. This is very doable because we can bring in foreign investment to complete that without putting any money there. It is business…” he said. Atiku also promised to continue the Baro Port project by dredging the River Niger, saying the port could serve states beyond Kogi and create jobs and economic opportunities. “Again, let me assure you, people of Kogi State, we shall continue the project of the Baro Port by dredging the River Niger, so that Baro Port can also serve other states of Nigeria. So you can imagine Baro Port being an equivalent of Apapa Port. It would bring about tremendous job opportunities and prosperity for the people of Kogi State and the entire Northern states.” The former vice-president has previously described his subsidy plan as support for locally refined fuel to reduce production costs and make petrol more affordable, rather than a return to subsidising imported fuel. Vanguard reported that he said the policy was intended to reduce fuel and transport costs. item.title: Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries
item.description: Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, has urged the UN management to urgently resolve 216 outstanding audit queries, stressing the need for greater accountability, transparency and compliance with established financial rules and procedures. Ibrahim made the call during deliberations of the UN General Assembly’s Fifth Committee on reports of the United Nations Board of Auditors, where he expressed concern over the number of unresolved audit issues and called for improved performance by the organisation’s management. He acknowledged that 100 audit reports had been cleared but said the 216 outstanding reports remained a significant concern that required urgent attention. Although he recognised that some of the cases might have been overtaken by events, the Nigerian diplomat urged the UN management to improve its clearance rate, which currently stands at 55 per cent. Ibrahim also emphasised the importance of timely payment of assessed contributions by member states, insisting that payments should be made according to schedule and translated into tangible benefits. On financial reporting, he stressed that the accuracy and integrity of data were fundamental to the credibility of reports presented before member states. ﻿ He said all stakeholders had a collective responsibility to safeguard the integrity of information underpinning the UN’s financial reporting. The Nigerian envoy warned that continued explanations without corresponding compliance could leave the organisation trapped in an endless cycle of justifications. He, therefore, urged UN management to prioritise adherence to established financial rules and procedures as the most effective way to address recurring audit concerns. Ibrahim also commended the cooperation between information-gathering systems and audit teams, describing their coordination as essential to improving the quality and reliability of UN reports. Meanwhile, the Fifth Committee considered the Secretary-General’s report on the estimated use of the commitment authority for 2026 and the proposed 2027 subvention to the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia. Speaking on behalf of the Group of 77 and China, Uruguay reaffirmed the group’s support for the proposed subvention, as well as its commitment to justice and national reconciliation. The Committee subsequently concluded its general discussion, with Canada’s representative, Sophia, expected to lead informal consultations to consolidate the observations and contributions of delegations. The Committee is scheduled to reconvene on November 30, 2026. The post Nigeria Urges UN To Clear 216 Outstanding Audit Queries appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: NASS Approves Tinubu’s $20.5bn, €1.45bn Supplementary External Borrowing Plan
item.description: The National Assembly has approved President Bola Tinubu’s request for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.517 billion and €1.45 billion for 2026 and 2027. The Senate approved the request on Tuesday following consideration of the recommendations of its Committee on Local and Foreign Loans. The approval came after the House of Representatives also endorsed the President’s borrowing plan. This file photo shows the red chamber of the Nigerian Senate. The proposed borrowing was calculated at an exchange rate of ₦1,400 to the dollar. Earlier on Tuesday, President Tinubu wrote to the Senate, seeking approval for a revised 2026 budget that reduces the previously approved expenditure by more than ₦3 trillion. The proposal, titled ‘Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Re-enactment Bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework’, was presented during plenary by Senate President Godswill Akpabio. House of Reps. (Photo by Facebook/House of Representatives, Federal Republic of Nigeria) Akpabio subsequently referred the correspondence to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for legislative consideration. Under the revised fiscal framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at ₦65.176 trillion, down from the ₦68.323 trillion earlier approved by the National Assembly. Projected Federal Government revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion, while capital expenditure is pegged at ₦26.232 trillion. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. Despite the reduction in overall expenditure, the fiscal deficit remains unchanged at ₦31.457 trillion, representing 5.64 per cent of the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The proposed new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion also remains unchanged. This comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic borrowing and ₦10.790 trillion in external borrowing. Tinubu explained that the proposed $7.7 billion external loan, estimated at ₦10.368 trillion, would finance an existing foreign borrowing provision and would not increase the overall borrowing limit. According to the President, the adjustments are intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation while maintaining fiscal discipline. The development comes amid expectations that Tinubu will present the 2027 budget to the National Assembly before the end of December. item.title: Peter Obi Lacks Competence To Lead Nigeria, Tinubu 100% Better — Abure
item.description: Former National Chairman of the Labour Party, Julius Abure, has said the party’s former presidential candidate, Peter Obi, lacks the character and competence to lead Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu is “100 per cent better”. Abure said he would not support Obi’s presidential ambition in the 2027 general election, citing his experience working with the former Anambra State governor and the internal crisis that fractured the Labour Party. He made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , where he explained why he considered Tinubu a better choice among the leading contenders for the presidency. Abure was a key ally of Obi during the 2023 presidential campaign and campaigned extensively for him. However, Obi subsequently left the Labour Party following a protracted leadership crisis. He blamed Obi’s caretaker committee decision for deepening the Labour Party’s crisis, driving elected officials away and raising questions about his leadership. “If indeed Obi was a good leader, why did they not follow Peter Obi? Peter Obi doesn’t have the character and competence to lead the country; we are sorry to say. Given my experience, I now know better,” he said. Peter Obi and Julius Abure appear in court for the presidential election petitions tribunal on Friday, June 2, 2023 Asked whether his decision to campaign extensively for Obi in 2023 had been a mistake, Abure admitted that it might have been. “Yes, it may have been an error because I now know better. Experience, they say, is the best teacher. Now I have experienced working with Peter Obi and that he is unstable, unreliable, a pretender who cannot be trusted because of the way he treated the leadership of the party,” he said. ﻿ Asked whether he still considered Obi “a saint,” Abure declared his support for Tinubu, describing the president as a more suitable candidate. “President Bola Tinubu is 100 per cent better. Today, we have the right to support whatever candidate we want. Obviously, Peter Obi is out of the question for us to support, given our experiences with him. We made a critical analysis of all the candidates: Tinubu, Atiku and Obi. “We feel Tinubu is the best candidate for us to support, given his trajectory so far in office and his ability to resolve conflicts compared to Peter Obi. The stage we are in now requires someone who can bring people together because the country is more divided than ever before. We need a bridge-builder who can unite people, and I do not believe Peter Obi has that capacity at this critical time in our history,” he said. He, however, dismissed allegations that he was responsible for Obi’s departure from the Labour Party, describing such claims as a “clear misconception”. item.title: ‎After Daily Trust story, foundation sponsors surgery for Kano teen battling facial tumour
item.description: ‎The Ihsan Scholarship Foundation, Kano, has sponsored the life-changing surgery of Salisu Sani, an 18-year-old whose struggle with a debilitating facial tumour was highlighted by Daily Trust, restoring hope to the teenager and offering him a chance to rebuild his future. ‎‎Daily Trust had reported how Salisu Sani, an indigene of Yalwa town in Tofa Local Government Area of Kano State, spent his days along Gandun Albasa Street in Kano soliciting support for a critical surgery after a massive tumour on his face left him in constant pain and threatened his eyesight. ‎‎Following the publication, a Kano-based foundation known for its humanitarian and educational interventions reached out to the teenager and took over the responsibility of his treatment. ‎The foundation, which requested anonymity, facilitated his return to the [Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (AKTH), where medical evaluations were conducted and the much-needed surgery was successfully carried out. ‎Medical records obtained by Daily Trust showed that specialists at the hospital diagnosed the condition as Aggressive Trabecular Ossifying Fibroma, a rare fibro-osseous tumour affecting the jaw and facial bones. ‎The pathology report indicated that tissue samples removed during surgery weighed about 640 grams. ‎‎Family members expressed gratitude to the foundation, medical personnel and members of the public who showed concern after the story was published. ‎Speaking after the successful operation, Salisu Sani said the intervention had given him a new lease of life. ‎“I never imagined that help would come this fast. For years I lived with the pain and the burden of carrying this tumour on my face. Today, I feel hopeful again,” he said. ‎The teenager had earlier told Daily Trust that the illness had forced him out of school and shattered his dreams, as his family could not afford the cost of treatment. ‎In a further boost to his recovery and future, the foundation also pledged to support his long-term rehabilitation by either sponsoring his education or providing him with full startup capital to establish a business and become self-reliant. ‎‎A representative of the foundation said the decision was informed by the need to ensure that the teenager not only receives medical care but also has the opportunity to build a productive life after recovery. ‎‎“Our concern is not limited to the surgery alone. We want him to be able to stand on his own feet and pursue his dreams. Whether through formal education or entrepreneurship, we will support him to become self-reliant,” the representative said.
